skill.name: swarm
skill.description: Autonomous multi-agent workflow system for complex coding tasks. It creates structured plans, runs iterative agents, and uses review gates before completion.
skill.summary: Coordinate autonomous coding agents with shared plans, review gates, and completion checks.
skill.author: nbashaw

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown formatting, normal shell bookkeeping, or local test harness behavior. A real issue remains: the skill intentionally launches autonomous Codex or Claude agents with reduced permission checks, and the test script uses a predictable temporary file path.

remediation.issue: Autonomous agents run with full-auto or permission-bypass flags.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each agent run, avoid permission-bypass modes by default, and document the exact workspace scope before execution.

remediation.issue: The shell runner directly launches local AI CLIs from the workflow script.
remediation.suggestion: Add a safe dry-run default, require an explicit unsafe flag for autonomous execution, and print the exact command before running it.

remediation.issue: The test script uses a predictable file name under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp for the test plan file and clean up the exact path created by mktemp.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Agent Execution With Permission Bypass
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to run headless agents with Codex full-auto mode or Claude permission bypass. The script directly launches those modes, allowing autonomous file edits and command execution with reduced approval barriers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly names full-auto and permission-bypass modes, and the shell script invokes them directly. This is intentional autonomous execution, not a weak pattern match.

content.value_statement: Large coding tasks can lose context across many steps. Swarm turns the work into a shared plan and runs agents through review gates.
actual_capabilities: Interviews the user to define goals, scope, tests, and plan location.
Creates a structured markdown plan with phases, checkboxes, roles, and a shared log.
Runs a shell script that iterates Codex or Claude agents against the plan.
Uses reviewer, simplifier, tester, and gatekeeper roles during longer work.
Tracks completion with a workspace marker file after gatekeeper approval.
limitations: It is not suited for single-line edits, typo fixes, or simple configuration changes.
It depends on local Codex or Claude CLI availability and workspace permissions.
Autonomous execution can make broad file changes, so review is still required.
The script uses a local completion marker that can become stale between runs.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Subsystem
use_cases.description: Break a multi-file refactor into phases with testing and review checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Add Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Plan coverage work, run agents through implementation, and require pasted test output before completion.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Migration
use_cases.description: Guide agents through staged modernization work, such as moving APIs or changing async patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Medium Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a bounded coding change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm to plan this task. Ask me for the goal, affected files, tests, and where to store the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Run With Review Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the task touches several files and needs verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm for this feature. Include reviewer, tester, and gatekeeper steps before marking the work complete.

prompt_templates.title: Resume an Existing Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue work after previous iterations or an interrupted session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume swarm from the existing plan file. Read the latest log, identify the next unchecked step, and continue safely.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Agent Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use after autonomous iterations have completed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the completed swarm plan. Verify the gatekeeper evidence, inspect the final changes, and list any remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Use swarm to refactor the authentication module and add tests.
output_examples.output: A scoped plan with refactor phases, test commands, review roles, and a gatekeeper checklist.

output_examples.input: Resume the migration plan from yesterday and finish remaining steps.
output_examples.output: A status report from the latest plan log, followed by the next iteration steps and verification results.

output_examples.input: Check whether the autonomous work is ready to merge.
output_examples.output: A concise readiness summary covering tests, changed files, gatekeeper evidence, and unresolved issues.

best_practices: Start with a precise goal, affected paths, and exact verification commands.
Review the plan before starting autonomous execution.
Inspect the final diff and test output before merging changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use swarm for trivial edits that need one direct change.
Do not run autonomous agents on unclear goals or open-ended exploration.
Do not treat the completion marker as proof that the code is correct.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It coordinates autonomous coding agents through a shared plan, review roles, and a completion checklist.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It documents support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for substantial coding work that benefits from planning, iteration, testing, and review gates.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for typo fixes, single-file edits, simple configuration updates, or tasks needing frequent decisions.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The included script can launch local Codex or Claude CLI processes and should be reviewed before use.

faq.question: Does completion mean the work is ready?
faq.answer: No. Completion means the workflow ended. You should still inspect changes, logs, and verification output.
